subject: audited response stream completion and protocol framing
findings: Hyper H1 drops the user body when its encoder no longer allows more bytes; fixed-length framing can reach that state before an async wrapper is polled for upstream EOF and terminal audit.
HEAD, 204 and 304 are protocol-bodyless; their outgoing body may never be polled.
reqwest content_length is the actual body size hint rather than the raw Content-Length header. A known zero body is positively polled for EOF before its terminal audit is acknowledged.

Full workspace object_store enables reqwest/http2. The original raw Hyper service returned a nonempty HEAD body, unlike Axum which sets representation length then removes the HEAD body. The explicit HTTP2 focused test reproduces that invalid fixture response as 502; the corrected fixture sends no HEAD data and retains its representation length. Credentials now explicitly enables the same upstream HTTP2 feature.
scope: Actual TLS regression confirms nonempty fixed-length, zero-length, HEAD and 204 under H1 and H2. Synthetic packet authority is not native capability evidence.
